sections.overview: Prototroctes maraena is a slender, silvery fish endemic to south-eastern Australia.
sections.identification: Its fins have soft rays and no spines.
sections.habitat: Adults live in freshwater rivers and streams; larvae and juveniles use estuaries and coastal waters.
sections.diet: The Victorian fisheries authority describes its diet as probably omnivorous, including insect larvae, small crustaceans and plant matter.
sections.behavior: It migrates between freshwater and the sea during its life cycle.
sections.reproduction: Spawning occurs in freshwater; early stages drift downstream before juveniles return upstream.
sections.ecology: Barriers to movement and altered river flows can disrupt this migration and are recognised conservation pressures.
sections.conservation: It is listed as Vulnerable nationally in Australia and Endangered in New South Wales.
